## My Interactive Visualizations Portfolio

```{r echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
user <- "aakritixyz"
repos <- c(
  "ten-points-animint", "iris-animint-test", "worldbank-animint-test", 
  "kmeans-animint-test", "mc-sample-mean-test", "buffon-needle-test", 
  "rosling-bubbles-test"
)

# We are going to build the table as one giant string to prevent 
# R from breaking it up and Pandoc from seeing the URLs individually.
table_html <- "<table><thead><tr><th>Screenshot</th><th>Project</th><th>Links</th></tr></thead><tbody>"

for(repo in repos){
  img  <- paste0("[https://raw.githubusercontent.com/](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/)", user, "/", repo, "/main/Capture.PNG")
  demo <- paste0("https://", user, ".github.io/", repo, "/")
  code <- paste0("[https://github.com/](https://github.com/)", user, "/", repo)
  name <- toupper(gsub("-animint|-test", "", repo))

  row <- paste0(
    "<tr>",
    "<td><img src='", img, "' width='200'></td>",
    "<td><b>", name, "</b></td>",
    "<td><a href='", demo, "'>Demo</a><br><a href='", code, "'>Source</a></td>",
    "</tr>"
  )
  table_html <- paste0(table_html, row)
}

table_html <- paste0(table_html, "</tbody></table>")

# This is the magic part: knitr::asis_output protects the string
knitr::asis_output(table_html)
